home.title: Hallstream: stream your club’s home games to YouTube
home.description: A free, open-source Windows app for basketball clubs. It reads the score from the hall’s Stramatel console or a phone, puts it on the stream in your club’s colours, and sets up OBS and YouTube.
home.h1: Your club’s home games, live on YouTube.
home.coverAlt: Hallstream on air: the Classic score bug and a player lower third over a basketball court
home.coverCaption: On air with the Classic look: the score bug, and a lower third for the player who just scored.
home.lede: One person runs it on the hall’s PC. It reads the score from your scoreboard console, draws the graphics in your club’s colours, and sets up OBS and the YouTube broadcast. There’s no account to make, and no tracking.

source.intro: Hallstream reads the score from the hall’s console when there is one. A phone at the scorer’s table covers every other case.
source.console: A Stramatel Stream Box, paired over Bluetooth. Score, clock, fouls and timeouts arrive on their own.
source.phoneH3: From a phone at the scorer’s table
source.phone: Held sideways, on the scoring page. It also takes over if the console drops out mid-game.
source.scorerAlt: The phone scoring page held landscape, with points, clock, fouls and timeouts, and the clock running
source.scorerCaption: The scoring page with the clock running. Points, fouls and timeouts are one tap each.
source.youthAlt: A youth basketball game in a sports hall, a coach with the ball and parents on the benches

rows: Reads the score, clock, fouls and timeouts from the hall’s Stramatel Stream Box over Bluetooth. The score bug follows the scoreboard.
Score bug, player and commentator lower thirds, opener, time-out, half-time, final result, sponsors, next game and “we’ll be right back”, in your club’s colours.

Creates the live broadcast with its title and thumbnail. After the game it makes the video unlisted, so it stays at its link and off your channel’s front page. Streaming somewhere else? Give it the RTMP server and key instead.
Switch screens from the browser on the hall PC, or from any phone on the same wifi with a PIN.
more: OBS Studio, the free streaming app, does the encoding. Install version 31 or later first. Hallstream sets it up over obs-websocket, with the scene, the overlay and the camera.
Type them in or import a CSV. Portuguese basketball clubs can pull both from the federation. The next fixture fills the “next game” screen.
After the first load, the graphics, the panel and the scoring page keep working if the hall’s internet goes.
Plays an invented game with no console attached, so you can learn it at home before Saturday.
The app speaks European Portuguese and British English. Pick one in the first-time setup or in Settings. Other languages can follow as community translations.

order.intro: A home game with a 19:00 tip-off, as one volunteer runs it from the hall’s PC.
steps: Download Hallstream onto the PC in the hall and open it. Try demo mode once, so the panel is familiar on the night.
Turn on obs-websocket. Hallstream builds the scene, the overlay and the camera.
Choose tonight’s fixture from your list, typed in, imported or pulled from the federation.
Hallstream creates the YouTube broadcast. Put the opener on screen while the teams warm up.

consoles.title: Supported consoles: which scoreboards Hallstream reads
consoles.description: Hallstream reads Stramatel scoreboards through the Stramatel Stream Box over Bluetooth, tested on real basketball games. Any hall can keep the score on a phone instead.
consoles.answer: Hallstream reads the score, clock, fouls and timeouts from Stramatel scoreboards through the Stramatel Stream Box, over Bluetooth, and that is tested on real basketball games. A hall without a supported console can keep the score on a phone at the scorer’s table instead; that page is new and has not been used at a game yet. Daktronics AllSport, Fair-Play and Bodet consoles, over serial RS-232, are on the roadmap.
rows: Stramatel scoreboards, through the Stramatel Stream Box
Stramatel Stream Box, handball, volleyball and hockey modes
Any console, or none: a phone at the scorer’s table, on the scoring page
Basketball. Other sports when they ship.

status.ready: Codes read, needs a recorded game

consoles.missing: Hallstream learns a console by reading what it sends during a game. To add one, a contributor needs to know the make, the model and how it connects, and later a recording of a real session to test the decoder against. The roadmap has a capture mode that records a session straight from the console. Until it ships, open an issue with the details below. The Stream Box handball, volleyball and hockey modes each need one recorded game before they count as tested.
consoles.stepsAfter: with the console’s make and model.
steps: Say how it connects (Bluetooth, serial, or a box in between) and which sports your hall runs on it.
Later, once capture mode ships, record one game and attach the file to the issue.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: What hallstream.com and the Hallstream app collect: cookieless visit counts on the site, and in the app only what you connect it to.
privacy.intro: Hallstream sends nothing to us. It talks to YouTube, the federation calendar and OBS only when you set them up. This site sets no cookies. Updated 25 November 2026.
privacy.site: Vercel Web Analytics counts visits. It records the page, the referring site, your country, and your browser and device type. It recognises a visit by a hash of the request that Vercel deletes after 24 hours, and it sets no cookies. There is no Google Analytics and no advertising.
privacy.hosting: The site is hosted on Vercel, which keeps the usual server logs (IP address, time, page) to run and protect the service.
privacy.app: The app has no account. It runs on the hall’s PC and keeps the club’s settings, squads, games and logs in its own folder, beside the program.
privacy.appSends: It connects to other services only when you set them up:
appList: YouTube, when you sign in to create broadcasts.
The Portuguese basketball federation’s data, through calendariofpb.pt, when a Portuguese club chooses to pull squads and fixtures from it.
OBS, on the same PC or network, over obs-websocket.
GitHub, once a day, to see whether a newer version is out, only if you turn on “Tell me when a new version is out” in Settings. It sends its version number and nothing about the club.

Hallstream’s feedback service, only when you send a message from Help. It files a public GitHub issue with your message, the version, the system, the scoring input and the sport, so write nothing personal in it.
privacy.logs: The source code can send each game’s logs to a server after the stream, but only when it is built with an upload key, and the public releases are built without one. A program built without the key writes that in its own log.
privacy.phone: The control panel and the scoring page can be opened from a phone on the hall’s wifi. That traffic stays on the local network and needs the PIN.
